theft_robbery.label: Theft / Robbery / Snatching
steps: Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. Mention the time, place and description of the item (for a phone: IMEI number).
If a phone or SIM was taken, ask your mobile operator to block the SIM and ask the police to record the IMEI.
Keep evidence safe: photos, medical papers, messages, call records, receipts and names/contacts of witnesses.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

assault_hurt.label: Physical assault / Hurt
steps: Get medical treatment first and ask the doctor to write down every injury (keep the prescription and medical certificate).

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer.
Keep evidence safe: photos, medical papers, messages, call records, receipts and names/contacts of witnesses.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

murder_homicide.label: Murder / Attempt to murder / Death by negligence
steps: Call 999 immediately if anyone is in danger or injured; do not disturb the scene.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. A family member or witness can be the informant.
Do not move or clean the place where it happened. Note names of witnesses.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

threat_intimidation.label: Threat / Intimidation / Blackmail
steps: Take screenshots or record calls/messages as proof of the threat, with date and time.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. If you feel in immediate danger, call 999.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

sexual_harassment_women.label: Sexual harassment / Eve-teasing
laws: Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Women and Children Repression Prevention Act)
steps: Move to a safe place. Call 999 if in danger, or the women and children helpline 109.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. You can also ask for a woman officer and a medical examination if needed.
Keep evidence safe: photos, medical papers, messages, call records, receipts and names/contacts of witnesses.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

rape_sexual_violence.label: Rape / Sexual violence
laws: Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Women and Children Repression Prevention Act)
Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Women and Children Repression Prevention Act)
steps: Your safety comes first. Call 999 or the helpline 109 and go to a safe person or place.

Do not wash or change clothes before the medical examination if you can avoid it; evidence matters. Go to a government hospital (One-Stop Crisis Centre / OCC where available) for examination and treatment.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

dowry_domestic_violence.label: Dowry / Domestic violence
laws: Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Women and Children Repression Prevention Act)
steps: If you are in danger, go to a safe place and call 999 or the helpline 109.
Get medical treatment for any injury and keep the medical papers.
You can file a case at the police station or apply to the court for a protection order under the Domestic Violence Act.
Keep evidence safe: photos, medical papers, messages, call records, receipts and names/contacts of witnesses.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

fraud_cheating.label: Fraud / Cheating / Breach of trust
steps: Collect all proof: receipts, bank/bKash/Nagad transaction records, chats, contracts and the person's identity details.
Send a written demand for return of the money if safe to do so, and keep a copy.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

cyber_crime.label: Cyber crime / Online harassment
steps: Take screenshots with date/time and copy the profile or post links BEFORE reporting; do not delete the evidence.
Report the content or account to the platform to get it taken down.
Report to the police station or the police cyber unit and ask for the case to be recorded under the cyber law. Women can also call 109.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

defamation.label: Defamation / False allegations
steps: Collect proof of the false statement (screenshots, recordings, witnesses) and who heard or read it.
Defamation is usually pursued by a complaint to the court; consult a lawyer on whether to file a case or send a legal notice first.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

illegal_arrest_police.label: Arrest / Police detention rights
steps: An arrested person must be told the reason for arrest, may meet and be defended by a lawyer of their choice, and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours (Article 33).
Contact a lawyer immediately and note the time and place of the arrest and the names of the police officers if possible.

If the person is held beyond 24 hours or tortured, tell the lawyer so they can apply to the Magistrate or the High Court Division (Article 102 writ, e.g. habeas corpus). Torture is prohibited by Article 35(5).
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

land_property_dispute.label: Land / Property dispute
steps: Collect your land papers (deed, khatian/record of rights, mutation, tax receipts) and take dated photos of the land.
If someone has entered or taken the land by force, report to the police and also consult a lawyer about a civil case (injunction or recovery of possession) in the civil court.
Check land records and mutation status at the local land office (AC Land / Union Land Office).
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

labour_dispute.label: Labour / Wage dispute
steps: Keep your appointment letter, ID card, pay slips, attendance records and any messages about wages.
Make a written complaint to the employer, then approach the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) or the Labour Court.
Workers' organisations and legal aid can also help. If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

consumer_issue.label: Consumer rights
steps: Keep the receipt, product, packaging and photos.
Complain to the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (hotline 16121) or the District Consumer office.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

kidnapping.label: Kidnapping / Wrongful confinement
laws: Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000 (Women and Children Repression Prevention Act)
steps: Call 999 immediately; time is critical. Give the last known place, clothes, photos and phone number of the person.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. Child or woman missing cases are treated seriously; also call 109 if relevant.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

road_accident.label: Road accident / Negligent driving
steps: Call 999 and get injured people to a hospital first.
Note the vehicle number, driver details and witnesses; take photos of the scene.

Report it at the nearest police station (GD or FIR). For a serious (cognizable) offence the police must record your information (CrPC Section 154). If they refuse, approach the Superintendent of Police or file a complaint before the Magistrate through a lawyer. Keep hospital papers for compensation claims.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.

drugs.label: Narcotics / Drug offence
steps: If you or a family member has been arrested, contact a lawyer at once; the right to a lawyer and to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours applies (Article 33).
To report drug dealing, contact the Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) hotline 16358 or the police. For addiction treatment, DNC runs treatment centres.
If you cannot afford a lawyer, call the government legal aid helpline 16430.
